note: Formula Systems' record Q3 (half of group revenue, +22% rev / +37% EBIT) was filed on an SEC 6-K hours before the seal, so the largest segment of an un-pre-released Q3 is known strong while the stock sits -16% in 20 sessions; capped by an unsourced Q3 bar, unknown Asseco Poland/International segments and this name's habit of selling its own beats (-2.65% on the Q2 beat).

Both items are public and traded through (the LOTF II slip two sessions ago on a 0.8% day, the KUKE-guaranteed refinancing 3.5 weeks ago); the only residual is the first document in which cost and cash to an April 2027 launch can be read against an Aug 2027 maturity, which is close to an honest zero.

An un-pre-released H1 on a name whose observed RNS reaction median is 16.8% (interims -14.8% and +28.9%), with consensus sitting exactly on the company's own >=GBP550m NOI floor; the CEO/64.6% holder bought ~GBP5m at 604-690p after the period closed and said the peers' low-vol headwind 'is not reflected in CMC's performance', and the tape has since given that whole signal back to 651p, so the upside case is not in the price.

The release carries the company's first 2027 guide, a scheduled guidance event on the European measurement (9% median) in a thin NOK name trading 28% below the June placement; sign held near 50 because the offsetting documented fact is that LTM pro-forma EBITDA of 188m already sits below the 190-230m 2026 guide with Microprecision loss-making, so a low-end narrowing is as likely as an on-path 2027 number.

The FY26 recurring-EBITDA-margin guide of 'close to last year' needs H2 near 24% after Q2 printed 22.6% on cost items that do not reverse in a quarter, and the sell-side has not marked down (6-analyst target ~197 vs spot 152.5, only Trigon cutting to 181); margin-led misses have been sold here (-8% and -3.8%) and the guide is the line the move lives on, but the bar is a third-party summary rather than a primary document.

Peak-quarter margin risk from fuel (Q2 EBITDA -5.1% on revenue +26%, Jet2's same summer -18% pre-tax) plus a ~-35m PLN unrealised FX mark on USD leases, both mostly modellable arithmetic and a peer proxy; held small because ENT has beaten the PAP EBITDA bar in Q3 2025 and Q2 2026 and the market reads through the below-the-line items.

The company itself said institutional fundraising timing 'remains an important factor in the delivery of near-term consensus expectations', and the consensus it published afterwards on 2 Nov still carries FY27 FUM at GBP10.7bn against GBP9.1bn actual at H1, so the interims are a likely softening or non-reaffirmation; the directly comparable event (Dec 2025 interims, in-line numbers, soft outlook) moved -11.3%, and a pre-print drawdown did not protect this name in October.

An 8.6% mover whose H1 LfL is pre-released and whose FY27 PBT range of GBP55-65m was reiterated, so the only live line is a possible narrowing with no sourced pointer either way; the 15% de-rating since the in-line October update resets the bar slightly positively, offset by a flat BRC October non-food backdrop for the first weeks of the H2 the company is already spending into.

Four of the six months are pre-released at revenue +9.8% with profit called 'in line', so the mover is the one forward paragraph, and the company's own August language (supplier price rises levelled out, customers slightly less confident) plus Travis Perkins' merchanting volumes at -9.0% in Jul-Sep point cautious; Howdens' +6.8% and Latham's share gains cut the other way, so the lean is small on a 1.2%-median name.

FY26 is pre-released as in line, so the reaction sits on the first ~8 weeks of FY27 against last year's +3.8% that drove +12.7%; the NIQ/CGA tracker MAB itself calls its market went flat in October (pubs +0.4%) while Fuller's, Young's and Wetherspoon all reported strong post-period trading, and the stock is still ~10% above its pre-close level, which leaves a small net negative rather than a call.

Revenue and EBITDA were pre-released on 13 Oct, so the only new content is the subsequent-events note: the Nasdaq acquirer's 30-day exclusivity lapsed around 16-17 Nov with no ESPI either way and the EGM dropped the series S issue that would have met the LOI's EUR 10m equity condition, which is a wide two-sided tail on a 49%-vol microcap rather than a direction.

The large y/y Q3 PBT fall is a consequence of a guide already cut in May and of Conference League rather than Champions League football, and this issuer's prior y/y declines inside a held guide were not sold (+5.1%); the stock trades on the 13 Oct FCK sale process, whose optionality is priced and on which the company has said it will not update, so this is a tail and not a sign.

FY26 EPS is effectively pre-released and was reconfirmed on 15 Oct, two weeks before the year end, and the one negative that is new to the sector (Big Yellow's October occupancy deterioration) has already taken SAFE down 7.7% against BYG's 4.4%; a Q4 trading update on a reconfirmed guide is the lowest-information event on this day.

Everything that changes the quarter was pre-announced: the USD 5M AstronauTx income (10 Aug, repeated in the Q2 report), its sale at GBP 3.36M (10 Nov) and the tesofensine discontinuation, which the market already reacted to with +4.8% on 6x volume on 24 Nov; a pre-revenue biotech with no guidance and no new pipeline datum in the report is an honest zero.

The promised 'future strategy' update for the enlarged post-Picton trust is the only unseen line, and with four directors buying at 40-41p and a ~30% discount the incentive points to disposals or a return measure; a 0.5-1% NAV markdown from CBRE's Q3 capital values barely registers on a name whose NAV prints have moved it under 1%, so the whole thing is small.

No szacunkowe-wyniki pre-release exists and the report was pulled forward to after the 25 Nov close, so the whole Q3 lands in this window; management's own H1 document says the 100% oncology-follow-up payment (backdated to 1 Apr), the 2.68% CT/MR limit rise and 3% PET pricing help later quarters more, and Q3 is the first full quarter of all three on a $0.3m/day name that has risen 11% and 6.8% on its last two beats, against a documented 50%-overperformance headwind the 14% drawdown looks to be pricing.
